title: Frankl's even-parity conjecture for t-intersecting k-Sperner families
statement:
Let $n$ and $t$ be integers with $n+t$ even and $n>t$, and let ${\mathcal F}\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ be a **$t$-intersecting** family, meaning that $|F\cap F'|\geq t$ for all $F,F'\in{\mathcal F}$, and a **$k$-Sperner** family, meaning that it contains no chain of $k+1$ distinct sets under inclusion. **Frankl's conjecture.** One has

$$
|{\mathcal F}|\leq\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\binom{n}{\frac{n+t}{2}+i}.
$$

The bound is tight if true, attained by $\bigcup_{i=0}^{k-1}\binom{[n]}{\frac{n+t}{2}+i}$.
source_name: József Balogh, William B. Linz and Balázs Patkós, “On the sizes of t-intersecting k-chain-free families”, arXiv:2209.01656 (2022).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.01656

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2022).
